name: Apollo 11 Lunar Module 'Eagle' (descent stage)
status: Descent stage still at Tranquility Base. The ascent stage was jettisoned into lunar orbit and probably crashed within 1-4 months.
science: Carried the first humans to the Moon; they brought back 21.55 kg of lunar rock and soil and set up a seismometer and a laser reflector.
story: Hi, I'm Eagle, the Apollo 11 Lunar Module! On 20 July 1969 I carried Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin down to the Moon, and Neil radioed home: 'The Eagle has landed.' My top half flew them back to orbit, but my bottom half is still sitting at Tranquility Base, right where the first humans walked on another world.

name: Opportunity rover (MER-B)
status: Silent since a global dust storm in June 2018; mission declared over in February 2019.
science: Found rocks and minerals such as hematite that formed in water, evidence that Mars once had liquid water. Drove more than 45 km.
story: I'm Opportunity, a solar-powered rover. Scientists hoped I would work for 90 days, but I explored Mars for more than 14 years and found rocks that formed in water long ago! In June 2018 a giant dust storm covered my solar panels, and I have been quiet ever since.

name: Voyager 1
status: In interstellar space since about 25 August 2012, the first human-made object to get there.
science: Flew past Jupiter (5 March 1979) and Saturn (12 November 1980) and is now measuring the space between the stars.
story: I'm Voyager 1, launched in 1977 to visit Jupiter and Saturn. On 14 February 1990 I turned around and took the first 'family portrait' of our solar system, and I carry a golden record full of sounds and pictures from Earth. Today I'm the first spacecraft ever to travel through interstellar space, the space between the stars!

name: Apollo 15 Lunar Module 'Falcon' (descent stage)
status: Descent stage still at Hadley-Apennine. The ascent stage was crashed into the Moon on purpose on 3 August 1971.
science: Carried the first Lunar Roving Vehicle. The astronauts covered 27.9 km and brought back 77.31 kg of rock and soil, and their ALSEP science station sent data until 30 September 1977.
story: I'm Falcon, the Apollo 15 Lunar Module. In July 1971 I carried astronauts Dave Scott and Jim Irwin, and the very first car ever driven on the Moon, the Lunar Roving Vehicle! Before leaving, Dave dropped a hammer and a feather side by side, and with no air to slow the feather down, they hit the ground at the same time.

name: Viking 1 Lander
status: Silent since contact was lost on 13 November 1982. Renamed the Thomas Mutch Memorial Station in 1981.
science: Studied the biology, chemistry, weather and soil of Mars, and sent back the first picture from its landing site 25 seconds after touchdown.
story: I'm the Viking 1 Lander, and I touched down on Mars on 20 July 1976. Just 25 seconds after landing, I started sending home my very first picture of the Martian ground! I scooped up soil and watched the weather for more than six years, until my last contact on 13 November 1982.

name: InSight lander
status: Silent since its last transmission on 15 December 2022; mission declared over on 21 December 2022.
science: Studied the inside of Mars (its core, mantle and crust) with a seismometer, a heat-flow probe and precise radio tracking.
story: I'm InSight, a lander built to listen to the inside of Mars, a bit like a doctor with a stethoscope. My seismometer listened for marsquakes, but my digging 'mole' only got about 40 cm down instead of 5 metres, because the soil was too tricky! In December 2022 my solar power ran too low, and I went quiet.
